title: First 12 Weeks Impact Plan and Skills Checklist
doc_description: Working playbook for bringing new individual contributors (ICs) up to speed in their first 12 weeks with a focus on measurable impact, skill checkpoints, and tailored interview rubrics for re-runs during hiring calibration.
hiring_plan_summary: This note outlines a 12-week activation plan that complements existing hiring pipelines. For mid-senior IC hires (L3-L5) we expect role-specific measurable outcomes by week 12. Hiring plan changes here: (1) add a short take-home microproject for serving-runtime roles focused on latency regression identification, (2) standardize interview rubric language across panelists using concrete example prompts, and (3) require candidate read receipt of the 12-week plan in offer packet.
interview_rubric: System Design (30%) - Score 1-5. Look for clear tradeoffs, explicit lat/throughput constraints, KV cache considerations, and fallback policies. 1 = no structure, 3 = basic architecture, 5 = concrete sharding/caching choices and failure modes handled.

Coding/Problem Solving (25%) - Score 1-5. Evaluate correctness, clarity, and edge-case handling. Prefer small, testable solutions and concise reasoning about complexity and memory use in persistent caches.

Production Judgment (20%) - Score 1-5. Candidate shows experience shipping features: rollout plan, monitoring signals, mitigation for regressions, and cost tradeoffs (batching vs latency). 5 = specific rollout metrics and rollback criteria.
Communication & Collaboration (15%) - Score 1-5. Focus on clarity of tradeoffs to PMs/infra teams, ability to write a short postmortem, and responsiveness to feedback in mock PR comments.

Domain Knowledge (10%) - Score 1-5. For serving-runtime candidates: attention mechanisms, KV cache semantics, quantization tradeoffs, and common kernel-level bottlenecks. 5 = can sketch optimizations and expected latency impact.
Calibration note: interviewers should provide one concrete example for each score point when filling feedback. Use the example prompts in linked_artifacts to align expectations.
onboarding_checklist: Pre-day: access request ticket created and approved (VPN, GitHub, Slack, cloud project, CI accounts)
Day 1: welcome + team intro, run local dev environment tutorial, clone main monorepo, run unit tests
Week 1 goals: ship a small doc update or tiny bugfix that exercises CI and review flow; schedule 1:1 with manager & buddy
Week 2 goals: complete core product primer reading list and pair on triage rotation (bugs/alerts)
Weeks 3-4: take ownership of a small scoped task (minor feature, perf test, or infra cleanup) and complete post-deploy checklist
Week 6 checkpoint: manager + buddy review focusing on technical depth and communication; update 12-week plan with concrete milestones
Week 8: run a lightweight benchmark (latency/throughput) for a targeted path and propose one optimization or experiment
Week 10: present a short demo to the team showing implemented work and learnings; collect feedback
Week 12: final impact review with manager documenting shipped items, metrics (latency delta, cost/savings), and 90-day extension plan
Ongoing: schedule monthly check-ins until six months, maintain a learning log and PR cadence goal
12_week_timeline: Week 0 (Offer): send candidate the 12-week plan, sample tasks, and reading list; confirm buddy
Weeks 1-2: orientation + low-risk contributions; focus on repo literacy and public infra services
Weeks 3-4: scoped task ownership; initial performance baseline captured
Weeks 5-6: mid-point review + ramp decisions (need more pairings or refocus objectives)
Weeks 7-9: execute optimization experiment or feature; measure outcomes vs baseline
Weeks 10-11: consolidation, documentation, and knowledge transfer
Week 12: impact review and career-path conversation; convert to ongoing 90-day objectives
open_questions: Should mid-senior IC offers include a mandatory 1-week onsite pairing session? pros/cons for distributed teams?
What minimum metric do we require for a Week 12 'impact' pass for infra/serving roles (e.g., measurable latency improvement, production bug fix count, or documentation ownership)?
Can the take-home microproject be run as a timed interactive pairing to reduce plagiarism?
